A.why: Sun-hand crown and sun-disc pendant suit the zone, but the dark full-width block sleeves dominate the top view and the stepped skirt is a squat plinth.
A.fix: Slim the sleeves and re-tone them pale; make the stepped skirt widen from a narrow hip.

B.why: The most Grashan silhouette (ziggurat crown, stepped temple tiers), but the slab sleeves wider than the shoulders make it a walking building, not a woman.
B.fix: Use narrow single-column sleeves and a tapered bodice; use fewer, taller skirt tiers so it reads as a bell.

C.why: Straight column skirt with no flare, wide slab sleeves with high cuffs, and a weak diadem; reads as a robe or armour.
C.fix: Build an A-line or bell skirt from the hip, slim the sleeves and add a sun crown.

D.why: The rayed sun halo is the best sun-priestess read, and the V neck, belt and pleated fringe are pretty, but the skirt hangs straight and the sleeves are block-width.
D.fix: Splay the pleats into a real flare with a stepped stone hem; halve the sleeves; give the halo a dull-gold face.

E.why: Clean stone, gold and terracotta palette with a tiered skirt, but the boxy bodice and sleeves hold the width at the elbows, and the flat sun disc reads as a grey slab from behind and above.
E.fix: Narrow the sleeves and bodice; step the skirt out boldly from a narrow hip; give the disc rays.

F.why: The best skirt (a clean terracotta A-line from a belted waist) and a good beehive crown, but bright blue avatar showing through at the shoulders is off-palette and widens the shoulders.
F.fix: Cover the blue with slim pale sleeves; lighten the terracotta and add a pale hem band.

notes: No candidate meets the slim-sleeve requirement: every set still uses shoulder-width block sleeves. Graft ideas across sets: D's rayed halo and bodice plus F's A-line skirt plus B's stepped-stone hem language would make a strong candidate. Read from renders only; flat colours and haze ignored.
